summary: the case of tests/run grub under etude, against a bootctl grub that writes the tail in use, one that never rewrites the entry sector, a /dev/grubcore that admits a second opener, and one that stays held after its holder has closed it

argv: sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 utils && sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel utils/sbin/bootctl

faults.name: tail-in-use
faults.summary: bootctl grub writes the new core into the tail the entry sector already selects, the one the running GRUB was read from, so a write cut short would leave no core to boot

faults.name: entry-unwritten
faults.summary: bootctl grub writes and reads back the inactive tail and reports success without rewriting the entry sector, so the old core still boots

faults.name: two-openers
faults.summary: the kernel lets a second open of /dev/grubcore through while the first is held

faults.name: held-after-close
faults.summary: the last close of /dev/grubcore does not give the device back, so it stays busy after its holder has exited
